intro: Rank correlation captures monotone relationships without requiring a straight line. Tied observations need shared average ranks to avoid artificial ordering.
task: Replace both observation vectors by one-based average ranks, then return their Pearson correlation.
requirements: x and y are equal-length vectors containing at least two paired observations.
Give tied values the average of their occupied one-based ranks, then correlate centered rank vectors.
Reject constant rank vectors. Do not use the no-ties shortcut formula when ties occur.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Sort positions to discover groups of tied values, but write their shared ranks back to original positions.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: The average of the first and last occupied rank gives the rank for every member of a tie group.

explanation: Ranking discards the numerical gaps between ordered observations. Any strictly increasing transformation preserves the ranks and therefore preserves this correlation.
Ties occupy several positions but all receive the mean of those positions. Using arbitrary tie order adds information that the observations do not contain.
